title: Ghost usage correlation and retry suppression for accurate billing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We see intermittent 'ghost' billing events where retries, partial streams, or client timeouts cause multiple billed rows for what should be a single logical request. Existing approaches (global nonce, replay-tokens) reduce some duplication but don't cover: (a) multi-phase streaming sessions where partial tokens are committed asynchronously, (b) cross-region retries from SDK clients that re-establish without carrying server-assigned anchors, and (c) transient network partitions that cause at-least-once ingestion with missing client-side idempotency.

Goal: Implement a pragmatic server-first suppression & post-facto reconciliation system that: 1) prevents visible double-charges for common retry patterns within a bounded window, 2) provides deterministic, auditable receipts for committed consumption, and 3) reconciles rare edge duplicates offline with minimal customer impact and clear visibility. This ticket focuses on design + prototype of the runtime components and a staged rollout plan for the mitigation path.
acceptance_criteria: Server can attach a short-lived, globally unique consumption receipt ID to accepted requests and include it in responses for both streaming and non-streaming flows.
Runtime rejects immediate duplicate consumption when a matching receipt or high-confidence fingerprint arrives within the configured suppression window (default 90s).
Offline reconciliation job can detect and merge duplicate meter rows into a single billing record and emit an adjustment event with a human-readable reason and links to evidence.
Schema changes and new logs are backwards-compatible for existing downstream billing pipelines; no data loss during migration.
End-to-end tests that simulate cross-region retry, mid-stream reconnects, and client SDK double-send show no > 0.5% unexplained duplicates in a 10k request test harness.
technical_decisions: Introduce a lightweight server-generated consumption_receipt (UUIDv7-like) that is returned in response metadata and stored with the consumption record. Receipt TTL default 2 minutes and persisted idempotency window in memstore + RocksDB for crash recovery.

Fingerprinting: build a configurable fingerprint composed of (customer_id, route, short-request-hash, initial-kv-cache-checksum, client-timestamp) to increase matching confidence when receipts are absent. Use bloom filter pre-check to avoid expensive lookups at high QPS.

Suppression semantics: strong suppression first if receipt matches; probabilistic suppression if fingerprint matches above threshold and recent (within suppression window). Probabilistic path logs confidence and defers to offline reconciliation if uncertain.

Partial-stream handling: stream fragments will carry an ephemeral stream_token assigned at stream start. On reconnection, client presents stream_token to continue; server maps fragments to the original receipt until commit. If stream_token is lost, fallback to fingerprint + lookback merge.

Reconciliation: scheduled batch job that groups consumption rows by fingerprint +/- time window and applies deterministic merge rules (max-seen-tokens, prefer committed receipts). Produce adjustment records for downstream billing and a human-readable audit bundle.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy receipt + memstore suppression to a single low-traffic region (us-west-2 test tenant) with suppression window=30s, monitor duplicates metric and false-positive suppression rate for 72h.
Phase 1 (limited): expand to 10% traffic across regions, enable fingerprinting heuristics and bloom-filter pre-check. Keep reconciliation dry-run mode enabled (no billing adjustments, only alerts).

Phase 2 (enforce): enable deterministic suppression globally (receipt-first, then high-confidence fingerprint), start creating adjustment events but mark them as 'pending review' in the console for first 48h.
Phase 3 (reconcile): enable automated offline reconciliation adjustments after manual review period and ship dashboard+alerts for customer success to triage any contested adjustments.
testing_plan: Unit tests for receipt generation, TTL eviction, memstore crash recovery and RocksDB fallback paths.
Integration tests that simulate: immediate duplicate send, delayed retry from different region, mid-stream reconnect with stream_token and without stream_token.
Chaos test: kill memstore process mid-ingest and validate that receipts persisted to RocksDB prevent double-charges on restart.
Load test: 50k RPS synthetic traffic with 5% client-side random duplicate sends to measure false suppression and system overhead. Target <2% additional p95 latency and <0.5% unexplained duplicates.

2026-03-07 - SRE (review): Memstore eviction and crash-recovery procedure approved; please add a migration that rehydrates recent receipts on startup and a healthcheck that surface missing persistence windows.
